headline: Hawks fans dress the arena like a runway, then wait for the team to earn it.
summary: The Hawks crowd is Black Atlanta at its widest: longtime families, AUC alumni, Gwinnett and South Fulton suburbanites, transplants and corporate seats, all dressed for a runway. It's also the city's most erratic fandom, devoted in the Dominique years and indifferent in the lean ones. After 46-36 and a first-round loss to the eventual champion Knicks, fans are hopeful but wary. Reach them through local culture, not the logo.

insights.title: Black Atlanta is the real fan base
insights.detail: Atlanta's Black middle class, the AUC schools (Morehouse, Spelman, Clark Atlanta) and the hip-hop industry decide what is cool in the building. The MLK Day home game is the franchise's most culturally charged night of the year.
insights.implication: Build Hawks product with Atlanta Black creators and institutions, credited and paid. Make the MLK Day game the anchor launch, not a footnote.

insights.title: Loyal, light on ritual
insights.detail: The Hawks have no Garden-style ritual canon. Fans identify with eras (Dominique, the Pac-Man logo, Trae) more than with chants. Attendance and energy follow winning and star power.
insights.implication: Design around era nostalgia and player identity: the red-and-yellow Pac-Man hawk, Dominique's number 21. There is no single sacred symbol to protect or exploit.

insights.title: Jalen Johnson is the new face
insights.detail: Johnson is an All-Star and All-NBA player. Nickeil Alexander-Walker is the Most Improved Player, and Dyson Daniels and Onyeka Okongwu anchor a defense-first identity. Fans are moving from a Trae story to a team-defense story.
insights.implication: Make player-led capsules for Johnson and Daniels, with defense-flavored graphics. They fit the new identity better than the old high-scoring guard narrative.

insights.title: Gwinnett and South Fulton cheer differently
insights.detail: Metro fans range from Decatur, East Point and College Park on the south and east sides to the Gwinnett and North Fulton suburbs on the other. The commute to State Farm Arena is long, and MARTA is the equalizer.
insights.implication: Reach suburban families through Gwinnett and Cobb retail and school-age programming. Reach urban Gen Z through AUC, Little Five Points and Westside pop-ups.

insights.title: Retro is the loyalty currency
insights.detail: Fans treasure the 1970s-to-1995 Pac-Man hawk, the Dominique-era red and gold, and the City Editions honoring Atlanta culture and MLK. The new Specter uniforms put Atlanta among eight historic franchises.
insights.implication: Lead with heritage-informed throwbacks and the Specter collection, not novelty marks. Tell the Atlanta story in the details.

insights.title: Nike and Jordan are the default
insights.detail: Sneaker culture runs deep here, through local boutiques, resale and Jordan Brand's ubiquity. Nike and Jordan product is expected, not special. Credibility comes from local credit.
insights.implication: Work with local sneaker shops, DJs and artists, not broad advertising. The test is who is in the room.

places.name: State Farm Arena
places.why: The Hawks' home, renovated in 2018. Its club spaces and concourse make the gameday look as important as the game.

places.name: Atlanta University Center
places.why: Home of Morehouse, Spelman and Clark Atlanta, the style engine of Black Atlanta fandom and the center of homecoming season.

places.name: Little Five Points
places.why: The city's vintage, streetwear and counterculture corner, where throwback hawk logos and thrifted jerseys turn up.

places.name: Lenox Square
places.why: A long-running sneaker and fashion destination, where gameday outfits get bought.

places.name: Westside Provisions District
places.why: Design-forward retail and food, and a regular home for brand pop-ups aimed at the creative crowd.

places.name: Greenbriar Mall
places.why: A long-standing southwest Atlanta shopping hub with deep neighborhood sneaker and apparel roots.

places.name: Mercedes-Benz Stadium
places.why: Shares Downtown with the Hawks and anchors the Falcons and Atlanta United culture that competes for fan attention.

places.name: Atlanta Dream at Gateway Center Arena
places.why: The Dream's home in the southside suburb is a basketball hub for families and women's hoops fans who overlap with the Hawks base.

people.name: Jalen Johnson
people.why: The face of the franchise heading into 2026-27.

people.name: Nickeil Alexander-Walker
people.why: A breakout story fans hold up as the model of development.

people.name: Dyson Daniels
people.why: The defensive identity of the Snyder era.

people.name: Quin Snyder
people.why: Architect of a system that forces turnovers and shoots a lot of threes.

people.name: Dominique Wilkins
people.role: Hall of Fame forward and franchise icon
people.why: The Human Highlight Film is still the most beloved Hawk and a team ambassador.

people.name: Spud Webb
people.why: The 1986 dunk champion is still a local legend.

people.name: Killer Mike
people.why: A Westside-rooted voice for the city, with culture and business ties that make him a natural reference point.

people.name: Tony Ressler
people.why: The face of ownership, judged by fans on investment and direction.

moments.name: MLK Day home game
moments.why: Atlanta's traditional MLK Day game is the most culturally significant date on the Hawks calendar. It is tied to a reported City Edition tribute.

moments.name: Emirates NBA Cup group play
moments.why: East Group C (Boston, Charlotte, Chicago, Washington) opens at Boston on Oct 30 and gives the early season some stakes.

moments.name: Morehouse and Spelman homecoming season
moments.why: AUC homecoming puts alumni style and sneaker culture on Atlanta streets in the weeks before tip-off.

moments.name: Season opener
moments.why: With no opening-night or Christmas game, the home opener has to carry the launch energy.

moments.name: Specter uniform games
moments.why: Atlanta is one of eight historic franchises getting Nike's Specter uniforms.

moments.name: Playoff push
moments.why: Casual and bandwagon fans decide in the 2027 playoff run whether to show up.

vocabulary.meaning: Local shorthand for Atlanta, all over team and city branding.
An OutKast-rooted nickname for Atlanta's culture-defining outsiders. Use it with respect for the artists.
A dated nickname that locals use ironically. Keep it off lead product.
Area codes as identity: 404 for the core, 678 and 770 for the suburbs.
The regional hip-hop identity Atlanta helped define.
Dominique Wilkins' nickname, still used for the franchise's highlight-reel DNA.
The street name that is everywhere, from Peachtree Hoops to local identity.
The hawk cheer in team marketing. Fans are lukewarm on slogans.

designCues.cue: Pac-Man hawk red and yellow-gold from the Dominique era
designCues.source: The 1970s-to-1995 Pac-Man hawk uniforms fans still wear as throwbacks.
designCues.use: Use as a pop accent on warm-up and lifestyle pieces. The hex is approximate: confirm against the archive.

designCues.source: The core team color across eras.
designCues.use: Primary color for Association and Icon pieces and for Specter collection tie-ins.

designCues.cue: Hawk wing and Pac-Man hawk mark
designCues.source: The original 1970s-90s Pac-Man hawk logo and the current hawk head.
designCues.use: Put it on graphic tees and hoodies. Pair a heritage mark with a modern cut.

designCues.cue: Dominique number 21 and Human Highlight Film script
designCues.use: Numbered capsules and vintage-style lettering for the diehards.

designCues.source: The reported return of the 2020-21 City Edition honoring Martin Luther King Jr.
designCues.use: Work with the King family's licensing and Atlanta partners. Don't approximate the likeness or the speech.

designCues.source: Atlanta's peach identity and Georgia clay.
designCues.use: A secondary color for summer and lifestyle drops.

designCues.cue: Premium nylon and satin warm-up fabrics
designCues.source: The Atlanta gameday look favors tailored warm-ups, jewelry and statement outerwear.
designCues.use: Satin bombers and track sets with subtle hawk embroidery.

productHooks: Specter-uniform capsule with a hawk-wing tonal graphic and Dominique-number lettering, for heritage diehards.
MLK Day game collection made with local Black designers and the King family's approval, with the artists credited on the product.
Player-led apparel and signature-color footwear for Jalen Johnson and Dyson Daniels, in volt yellow and Hawks red.
Limited AUC homecoming and Westside pop-up run with local DJs, designers and sneaker shops, all credited.
Pac-Man hawk throwback shooting shirts and warm-ups in satin and nylon, for Atlanta's gameday-fashion crowd.
watchouts: MLK and civil-rights imagery needs the King estate's licensing and respectful treatment. Never use his words or likeness as a decorative graphic.
Hip-hop references (OutKast, Outkast-rooted slogans, lyrics) are third-party IP. License and credit them.
Atlanta is not one fan base. The Black urban core, Gwinnett and the corporate suburbs want different things.
Avoid trap or Magic City stereotypes. Engage artists and businesses as partners.
Trae Young's departure is still raw for some fans. Skip nostalgia product that reads as taking sides.

segments.name: Longtime Atlanta diehards
segments.description: Multigenerational Black Atlanta families and Dominique-era fans, many from southside and westside neighborhoods and the AUC.
segments.wears: Dominique-era red and gold, Pac-Man hawk throwbacks, Jordan Brand footwear, local streetwear.
segments.reach: Church, barbershops, AUC events, local radio and the MLK game.

segments.name: Suburban families
segments.description: Gwinnett, Cobb and South Fulton families who attend a few games a year.
segments.wears: Current Icon and Association jerseys, youth jerseys, licensed fleece.
segments.reach: Suburban retail, youth leagues and school partnerships.

segments.name: Gen Z digital fans
segments.description: Younger Atlantans and Georgia college students who follow the team on TikTok, Instagram and highlight accounts.
segments.wears: City Edition, oversized tees, Nike hoodies, Jordan sneakers.
segments.reach: Social creators, campus pop-ups and sneaker drops.

segments.name: Regional Georgia and Southeast fans
segments.description: Fans across Georgia, Alabama and the Carolinas, for whom the Hawks are the closest team.

segments.name: Corporate and club-seat fans
segments.description: Business-hospitality guests in Downtown and Buckhead, plus visitors from Atlanta's large corporate base.
segments.wears: Quarter-zips, premium polos, tailored jackets with team marks.

traditions.name: MLK Day home game
traditions.detail: The annual game on Martin Luther King Jr. Day is a cultural centerpiece, with community tributes and special apparel.

traditions.name: Gameday fit
traditions.detail: Fans treat arrival at State Farm Arena as a style moment: dressed-up streetwear, fresh sneakers, jewelry.

traditions.name: Dominique tributes
traditions.detail: Wilkins is honored in arena moments, and fans cheer his appearances louder than any current player.

traditions.name: Hip-hop in the building
traditions.detail: Atlanta artists turn up courtside and in halftime programming, and the arena soundtrack leans local.

icons.name: Dominique Wilkins
icons.why: The franchise's greatest scorer and the symbol of the Human Highlight Film.

icons.name: Pete Maravich
icons.why: Pistol Pete starred for Atlanta in the early 1970s, and older fans remember him.

icons.name: Spud Webb
icons.why: The 1986 Slam Dunk Contest winner, at barely five-foot-seven.

icons.name: Joe Johnson
icons.why: The star of the Hawks' playoff run in the late 2000s.

icons.name: Trae Young
icons.why: The star of the 2021 Eastern Conference Finals run. His era divides some fans.

rivalries.why: The Knicks beat the Hawks in the 2026 first round after Atlanta led 2-1, echoing the 2021 first-round series Atlanta won. The title-winning Knicks are the benchmark.
A Cup group rival and a playoff foe. The 2026-27 Cup opener is at Boston.
A Southeast Division rival. Postseason meetings have been sporadic.
Another Southeast Division opponent, with a young, defensive roster.
Past playoff series, and the traditional MLK Day opponent this season, with LeBron James as the draw.

extra.sentiment: Cautiously optimistic: a Jalen Johnson All-Star and a defense-first reload after a 46-36 season and a 2-1-series collapse against the Knicks. Many fans are still processing the Trae Young trade, and the Hawks must prove sustained playoff success.
extra.gamedayLook: Dressed-up streetwear with a jersey or hawk-logo piece layered in: red or black Icon jerseys, Dominique and Pac-Man throwbacks, fresh Jordan or Nike sneakers, caps, jewelry. Corporate seats add a quarter-zip or satin jacket.
